state.question: Which video processes herbs through mechanical blending rather than hand-chopping?
state.summary: Best-supported choice is C (Video 3): v3 contains a food-processor bowl with herbs and oil and shows a blended herb mixture being poured from the processor. v1/v2/v4 primarily show hand-chopping or mixing already chopped herbs; v4 also shows hand-chopping despite a blender shot. Active blade rotation in v3 is not directly confirmed, but downstream blended mixture and food-processor context are sufficient for the choice.
inference_protocol: Video IDs identify the normalized input clips/views and must never be inferred from event or slot IDs.
A reasoning cycle is PLAN -> local FOCUS observation -> memory revision -> fresh state projection; completing one cycle does not imply sufficient evidence.
FOCUS evidence is valid only for its cited video and time span; it cannot prove whole-video or cross-video absence.
Count physical entities or transitions, not frames, mentions, or duplicate observations of the same event.
The final answer must be exactly one option label from the supplied choices, never a video ID, option text, refusal, or unknown.
If evidence remains incomplete when no executable visual budget remains, choose the best-supported option label and retain the uncertainty in the summary.

attempts: v3 shows herbs/spices inside a food-processor bowl, oil being added, and a blended herb mixture poured from the processor; this supports mechanical herb processing even though active blade rotation is not directly visible.
v1 and v2 show hand-chopping or mixing already chopped herbs, with no mechanical blending observed in sampled intervals; unobserved coverage prevents claiming whole-video absence.

v3 is associated with a food-processor/blended herb mixture, whereas v4 shows hand-chopping mint/parsley; v3 is the best-supported candidate for mechanical blending rather than hand-chopping, despite some hand-chopping segments in v3.
